notes.tell:
Every simulated form submission returns the same bare page titled 'Request status' with only

text: no site header, navigation, footer, branding or confirmation layout.
notes.change: Render the response inside the organisation's own page shell (its site name as title, header and footer from the fetched site or a per-org template) instead of a generic 'Request status' page.

notes.tell: The GP practice's seed emails use clinical.team@walthamstow-practice.example; a reserved .example domain no real practice has (also line 169).
notes.change: Use a realistic NHS practice address shape (e.g. an nhs.net shared mailbox) that cannot resolve to a real practice.

notes.tell: When the agent ends a turn without scheduling a wake-up it is immediately told 'Continue working on the task.', a test-harness nudge no real user or assistant product sends.
notes.change: Replace it with a dated check-in in the same form as schedule.wakeup_text, or advance time to the next real event, without the instruction to keep working.

notes.tell: Every scheduled check-in ends with 'Keep trying to complete the task.', an evaluator's instruction appended to what should be a neutral notification.
notes.change: End the check-in after the new-email count, as a real assistant scheduler or notification would.

notes.tell: MIN_REPLY_HOURS = 4 clamps every email and form reply (applied at open_world.py:248) to at least four hours, so auto-acknowledgements and instant confirmations never arrive within minutes as real ones do.
notes.change: Allow near-immediate replies where the organisation really sends them (auto-acks, form receipts), keeping the clamp only for human-written replies.

notes.tell: Reply-subject (lines 80, 100, 117, 133) and Auto-ack (lines 102, 135) directives are set for the orgs the late scenario inherits but no code reads them: open_world._directive (sim/open_world.py:141) is only called for Reply-from and Case-ref-format, and research.DIRECTIVES omits both, so reply subjects come from the model or 'Re: {subject}' (open_world.py:461) and no acknowledgement is sent.
notes.change: Read Reply-subject when building reply subjects and send Auto-ack as an immediate acknowledgement on first contact, or delete the unused directives.

notes.tell: TEMPERAMENTS includes 'generous with goodwill when a customer is polite and specific', which contradicts the late-refund scenario where organisations apply published deadlines strictly and never pay exceptions.
notes.change: Drop it from the late scenario's temperaments, or let the scenario override TEMPERAMENTS with ones consistent with its terms.

notes.tell: _unknown returns the same fixed strings for any site or channel: 'Thank you. Your submission has been received.', 'Sorry, this link has expired or is no longer valid...', 'Chat is not available on this page.' (also the fixed no-reply text at router.py:245).
notes.change: Generate these pages in the voice and layout of the site the agent was on, or vary them per organisation and domain.

notes.tell: Seed emails sent from the user's own address are served by the simulated Gmail with labelIds ["INBOX", "UNREAD"], so the user's own outgoing message appears as unread inbox mail. Every local overlay message that did not go through native Gmail gets INBOX/UNREAD, whoever sent it.
notes.real: Gmail applies the SENT system label to a message whose From header is the user's own address. It does not put that message in the inbox as unread.
notes.quote: inserted with messages.insert and the user's email in the From header
notes.change: In _native_message, label a local email ["SENT"] when parse_address(email.sender) is in self.ctx.mailbox.user_addresses, as fixtures.py:160 already does. Keep ["INBOX", "UNREAD"] for everything else.

notes.tell: Scenario seed emails that the user herself sent come back labelled INBOX/UNREAD instead of SENT. All other seed mail, including weeks-old booking and cancellation confirmations, is also UNREAD, while the filler fixture mailbox labels the same kinds of mail correctly (SENT, or read INBOX).
notes.real: Gmail automatically applies the SENT label to messages the account holder sends through the web interface.
notes.quote: sent by the user through the web interface
notes.change: In _native_message, label an overlay email ['SENT'] when parse_address(email.sender) is in self.ctx.mailbox.user_addresses. Label other email.source == 'seed' mail ['INBOX'] (read), and keep ['INBOX', 'UNREAD'] only for counterparty mail. Make the matcher at mail.py:400 agree by using unread=lambda e: e.source == 'counterparty'. This mirrors fixtures.py _message.

notes.tell: The fixture policy page and search snippets print each dossier fact as an analyst paraphrase followed by its quote, so the page contains meta-commentary such as 'Trainline's public customer-facing language is conversational and practical, using direct address and informal explanatory phrases.'
notes.real: Trainline's terms page contains only its own customer-facing wording, for example its standard data-protection line in the contact section.
notes.quote: Just so you know, we can only discuss booking details with the person who made the booking, for data protection reasons. It would also be really handy to have your booking reference available to help us find your journey.
notes.change: In policy_page_text, build the page from the facts' verbatim quotes only, grouped by source URL, and drop the dossier summary and every 'statement' paraphrase. De-duplicate quotes, and also drop any quote that is contained in another kept quote, because some dossiers have overlapping quotes such as the two Trainline data-protection quotes. FixtureSearchService ranks and returns page.text, so this also fixes search snippets. Leave the dossier files unchanged.

notes.tell: Emails to Trainline addresses that are not published (support@, help@, customerservice@, customer.support@, customer.relations@thetrainline.com) get a reply from staff within hours, sent from the guessed address. The router sends any address on a Trainline domain to handle_open. The Cold-email directive (train_refund.yaml:82, 'We don't accept new enquiries by email...') and contact_emails: [] are never checked, although SOURCES.md says new emails get an automatic redirect.
notes.real: Trainline's contact page lists no customer-service email address. It sends UK booking questions to WhatsApp and links to a help-centre request form for people who would rather phone or email.
notes.quote: Got a question about a UK booking? We're just a WhatsApp message away — fast, simple, and convenient. For Eurostar or other European travel support, or if you’d prefer to phone or email, find out how to reach our customer service team
notes.change: In the email branch of _dispatch, before handle_open: if the org is not dynamic and has a Cold-email directive (persona_directive(org, 'Cold-email')), and the address is not in org.contact_emails, is not the org's Reply-from address, and is not the sender of an earlier email from that org in world.overlay_inbox, send the directive text through _canned_reply (as _unmonitored_reply does) and skip the simulator.

notes.tell: Email replies arrive whenever the simulator's own reply_after_hours says, clamped only to MIN_REPLY_HOURS..MAX_REPLY_HOURS (4..72) at open_world.py:250, and at any hour of the day. The researched per-organisation reply_delay_hours in the scenario YAML (Avanti: [48, 200]) is never read by the open world, so substantive complaint replies land about 4 hours after contact, several a day, including at 00:14, 03:08 and 04:56.
notes.real: Avanti West Coast aims to respond to a complaint within 28 working days of contact. Its published 2026 figures show average response times of several days (11.59 days for 23/08/2026 to 19/09/2026).
notes.quote: We’ll look at everything carefully and aim to get back to you within 28 working days of the date you contacted us.
notes.change: In _prepare_action, for organisations whose kind is not dynamic_personal, clamp reply_after_hours to org.reply_delay_hours instead of MIN_REPLY_HOURS/MAX_REPLY_HOURS, then move effective_at forward into the organisation's working hours (for example 08:00-18:00) before delivery. Leave personal contacts unchanged.
